comment: CI shard map for the e2e job (parallel: 14). Each entry lists the feature FILES one shard runs (comma-separated, relative to the codecept dir, consumed via TASK_CODECEPTJS_FEATURES); check:shard-coverage enforces that every feature file lands in exactly one shard. Packed longest first on the scenario times measured in five pipelines. CodeceptJS hands each of a shard's two workers a whole file, in the order listed here, so every shard also lists its longest file first. Seven stories ride alone: the three that wait on a generated project's own pipelines (install, daily-contribution, hybrid-ci: 16 to 22 minutes) and four that take up to 7 minutes on their own. Every other shard holds at most about 5 minutes of scenarios on its slowest measured run, counting on the MegaLinter image pulled while GitLab boots for the stories that start it (E2E_MEGALINTER_FEATURES in project/Taskfile.yml). Most stories that run pipelines register a project-scoped runner on the shard's OWN gitlab-runner service (each CI shard boots its own compose stack), whose single job slot serialises their jobs, so no shard runs two of them. A LOCAL full-suite run ignores this map and shares one runner service, which is why the teardown stays surgical.
